title: Open Source Must Be Fun (Or It Will Die)
excerpt: Homebrew is thriving while other open source projects struggle. Its scarcest resource isn’t money: it’s maintainer motivation.
content_html:
26 July 2026

I was on a call with a bunch of people involved in other prominent open source projects a few weeks ago. The organiser jokingly asked us to raise our hands if the previous six months had been better than what came before. I raised my hand. No one else did. Why? I’ve maintained Homebrew, the package manager for everywhere, for nearly 17 years. I’ve worked on it the vast majority of weeks in that time and I’ve never burned out. I’m having more fun than ever.

The current narrative around open source is depressing. Apparently it’s “dying”.

AI drive-by issues, pull requests and security reports are overwhelming maintainers. Rising security expectations (thanks Mythos) require maintainers to do even more work. Open source funding is hard to secure and insufficient.

Some of this is happening, but I’m sure as hell not seeing it in Homebrew. Another Homebrew maintainer told me:

I’m having more fun than ever before.

💎 The Scarcest Resource

As I’ve written before, the scarcest resource in open source is not money but the motivation of the maintainers. Sending Homebrew $1000 today doesn’t magically create any more maintainer time (but please donate if you can afford it to fund Homebrew’s infrastructure, stipends, grants and meetups). We all have jobs that aren’t maintaining Homebrew. We receive small amounts of money ($300/month) if we’re actively maintaining Homebrew. This is not a “market hourly rate”. Many children delivering newspapers get a higher hourly rate.

There is a threshold effect: funding only creates more time if it lets a maintainer reduce their paid hours or quit their job. Work no maintainer wants to do is a good candidate for a paid contract. If you can’t fund it: don’t do it.

Why do any of it then? Fun.

Not everything is fun all of the time, but it needs to be “utilitarian net fun”: more fun than not, overall. This is primarily about volunteer-run open source, but that’s most of it. If you have a paid open source job and hate it: you should quit that too.

It’s a Sunday afternoon. I took the kids most of yesterday so I have a bit of “me” time today. I’ve spent a bunch of that time on Homebrew. Not because I “had” to; nothing urgent is coming in. Not because of the “supply chain”. Not because of the money. Because I wanted to. Because it was fun.

My first real experience of OSS was with a successful, established project whose culture I could observe. It was KDE, the community behind a desktop environment for Linux. In 2009, I attended Akademy (the KDE contributor conference) and GUADEC (the GNOME contributor conference), which were co-located in the Canary Islands.

Firstly, this was weird because, if you read the discourse online, you were typically in the camp of “KDE SUCKS, GNOME ROCKS” or “GNOME SUCKS, KDE ROCKS”. And yet: you had both groups working together. Not just working together but eating, drinking, socialising and building new friendships.

Secondly, I could tell that, for many in the KDE camp, these were their people and this was the highlight of their year. They came back re-energised and motivated to work on KDE. Most people weren’t being paid to fix, maintain or write KDE’s code. They didn’t seem to be doing it for their users either. They did it because they were having fun, both individually writing the code and helping their friends build something they cared about.

For the last few years, Homebrew maintainers have met annually at the “Homebrew AGM” co-located with FOSDEM in Brussels. We meet, eat, drink, socialise and make plans for Homebrew. Afterwards, we come back re-energised. Since we started doing this, I’ve also seen people doing more for other maintainers than directly for users. Open source transcends national boundaries: most of us don’t care what country another maintainer is from or what nationality they are, only that we’re friends building something we find fun together. These relationships matter because, without the maintainers, the project is dead.

🍺 Keeping Homebrew Fun

This is why I’ve always been keen for Homebrew to be a fun project. Dealing with entitled behaviour is not fun. Setting SLAs is not fun. Maintaining indefinite backwards compatibility is not fun.

Homebrew has been successful because fun, automation, community and putting maintainers first have been priorities from early on. Concretely, we automated review comments so robots are the pedants and humans can focus on empathy. Our guardrails include CI, linting, typing and tests to catch routine mistakes before a maintainer has to point them out. Feature flags and staged rollouts let us experiment without breaking things for everyone. This means maintainers spend less time on repetitive corrections and more on work they find interesting.

AI is good at boring work like writing CI workflows, linters and documentation. These practices help both AI and human contributors. Maintainers can use or avoid AI, whichever better preserves their motivation.

If your eyes glaze over while reading low-effort AI-generated content: close it without comment or justification and block repeat offenders who do not learn or improve. At Homebrew, our pull request templates ask contributors to disclose AI usage and CI jobs automatically close pull requests with incomplete templates. Issues or PRs opened through the API without our templates often suggest AI usage with insufficient human involvement.

🛑 Stop, Pay or Quit

Homebrew is thriving, not dying. It has 28 active maintainers. Of the 29 maintainers it had a year ago, 26 remain. Under our governance rules, we remove maintainers after they miss an activity threshold for two consecutive quarters.

If your project is dying, maybe it’s because it’s not fun any more. You should quit. You don’t owe anyone anything. Homebrew maintainers are encouraged to leave without guilt or explanation.

If you don’t want to quit (or if you’re on a project where you don’t want others to quit) and things are going badly: change something. Don’t just ask for more money or sponsors or donations. That will not magically make things fun again. Getting more money is not in your locus of control.

Instead: stop doing the parts of your project that are not fun. Maybe that’s stable releases. Maybe that’s release notes. Maybe that’s backwards compatibility. Whatever it is: again, you don’t owe anyone anything. You can do OSS however the hell you want to do it.

People running soup kitchens don’t get constant complaints that the soup tastes like shit. They aren’t critiqued for not providing the optimum macronutrient balance. They do what they can. How sad is it, then, that some very well-compensated open source users with tech jobs treat volunteers so poorly?

⏭️ OK, What Now?

Are you a maintainer? If so, consider what keeps maintaining your project fun or what would make it fun again. If it isn’t fun and you can’t make it fun again: quit.

Are you a contributor? Ensure that you’re having fun contributing but not in a way that makes it less fun for the maintainers. If you’re submitting AI-generated content, carefully review and test it. Speak to the human maintainers instead of deferring to your LLM.

Are you a user? If you’re filing a bug report, take your time and provide all the requested information. Most importantly: be grateful for the gift of open source you’re getting for free. Keep your rants for the pub or coffee shop and off the internet. Drive-by negativity kills open source.

Are you a company consuming open source? Allow your employees to participate in Open Source Friday. Alternatively, look the other way when they participate in the Open Source Resistance. Sponsor some projects you rely on.

Keep having fun and the open source community will outlive us all.

Thanks to John Peebles, Graeme Arthur, Patrick Linnane, Andrew Nesbitt and Lindsay McQuaid for reviewing this post and providing helpful feedback.

sentences.en: Open source transcends national boundaries: most of us don’t care what country another maintainer is from or what nationality they are, only that we’re friends building something we find fun together.
sentences.zh: 开源超越国界：我们大多数人并不关心另一个维护者来自哪个国家或他们是什么国籍，只关心我们是朋友，一起构建我们觉得有趣的东西。

sentences.en: These relationships matter because, without the maintainers, the project is dead.
sentences.zh: 这些关系很重要，因为没有维护者，项目就死了。

blocks.html_en: 🍺 Keeping Homebrew Fun

sentences.en: 🍺 Keeping Homebrew Fun
sentences.zh: 🍺 保持自制的乐趣

blocks.html_en: This is why I’ve always been keen for Homebrew to be a fun project. Dealing with entitled behaviour is not fun. Setting SLAs is not fun. Maintaining indefinite backwards compatibility is not fun.

sentences.en: This is why I’ve always been keen for Homebrew to be a fun project.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我一直热衷于 Homebrew 成为一个有趣的项目。

sentences.en: Dealing with entitled behaviour is not fun.
sentences.zh: 处理正当行为并不有趣。

sentences.en: Setting SLAs is not fun.
sentences.zh: 设置 SLA 并不有趣。

sentences.en: Maintaining indefinite backwards compatibility is not fun.
sentences.zh: 保持无限期的向后兼容性并不有趣。

blocks.html_en: Homebrew has been successful because fun, automation, community and putting maintainers first have been priorities from early on. Concretely, we automated review comments so robots are the pedants and humans can focus on empathy. Our guardrails include CI, linting, typing and tests to catch routine mistakes before a maintainer has to point them out. Feature flags and staged rollouts let us experiment without breaking things for everyone. This means maintainers spend less time on repetitive corrections and more on work they find interesting.

sentences.en: Homebrew has been successful because fun, automation, community and putting maintainers first have been priorities from early on.
sentences.zh: Homebrew 之所以成功，是因为有趣、自动化、社区和将维护人员放在第一位，从一开始就是优先考虑的事情。

sentences.en: Concretely, we automated review comments so robots are the pedants and humans can focus on empathy.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，我们自动评论评论，这样机器人就可以成为学究，而人类可以专注于同理心。

sentences.en: Our guardrails include CI, linting, typing and tests to catch routine mistakes before a maintainer has to point them out.
sentences.zh: 我们的护栏包括 CI、linting、打字和测试，以便在维护人员指出之前发现常规错误。

sentences.en: Feature flags and staged rollouts let us experiment without breaking things for everyone.
sentences.zh: 功能标志和分阶段推出让我们能够在不破坏每个人的情况下进行实验。

sentences.en: This means maintainers spend less time on repetitive corrections and more on work they find interesting.
sentences.zh: 这意味着维护人员可以花更少的时间进行重复性修正，而将更多的时间花在他们感兴趣的工作上。

blocks.html_en: AI is good at boring work like writing CI workflows, linters and documentation. These practices help both AI and human contributors. Maintainers can use or avoid AI, whichever better preserves their motivation.

sentences.en: AI is good at boring work like writing CI workflows, linters and documentation.
sentences.zh: AI 擅长枯燥的工作，例如编写 CI 工作流程、linter 和文档。

sentences.en: These practices help both AI and human contributors.
sentences.zh: 这些实践对人工智能和人类贡献者都有帮助。

sentences.en: Maintainers can use or avoid AI, whichever better preserves their motivation.
sentences.zh: 维护者可以使用或避免人工智能，以更好地保持他们的动力为准。

blocks.html_en: If your eyes glaze over while reading low-effort AI-generated content: close it without comment or justification and block repeat offenders who do not learn or improve. At Homebrew, our pull request templates ask contributors to disclose AI usage and CI jobs automatically close pull requests with incomplete templates. Issues or PRs opened through the API without our templates often suggest AI usage with insufficient human involvement.

sentences.en: If your eyes glaze over while reading low-effort AI-generated content: close it without comment or justification and block repeat offenders who do not learn or improve.
sentences.zh: 如果您在阅读毫不费力的人工智能生成的内容时目光呆滞：请在没有评论或理由的情况下关闭它，并阻止那些不学习或改进的惯犯。

sentences.en: At Homebrew, our pull request templates ask contributors to disclose AI usage and CI jobs automatically close pull requests with incomplete templates.
sentences.zh: 在 Homebrew，我们的拉取请求模板要求贡献者披露 AI 使用情况，CI 作业会自动关闭模板不完整的拉取请求。

sentences.en: Issues or PRs opened through the API without our templates often suggest AI usage with insufficient human involvement.
sentences.zh: 在没有我们的模板的情况下通过 API 提出的问题或 PR 通常表明人工智能的使用缺乏人工参与。

blocks.html_en: 🛑 Stop, Pay or Quit

sentences.en: 🛑 Stop, Pay or Quit
sentences.zh: 🛑 停止、付款或退出

blocks.html_en: Homebrew is thriving, not dying. It has 28 active maintainers. Of the 29 maintainers it had a year ago, 26 remain. Under our governance rules, we remove maintainers after they miss an activity threshold for two consecutive quarters.

sentences.en: Homebrew is thriving, not dying.
sentences.zh: 自制啤酒正在蓬勃发展，而不是消亡。

sentences.en: It has 28 active maintainers.
sentences.zh: 它有 28 名活跃维护者。

sentences.en: Of the 29 maintainers it had a year ago, 26 remain.
sentences.zh: 一年前有 29 名维护者，现在只剩下 26 名。

sentences.en: Under our governance rules, we remove maintainers after they miss an activity threshold for two consecutive quarters.
sentences.zh: 根据我们的治理规则，我们会在维护者连续两个季度未达到活动阈值后将其删除。

blocks.html_en: If your project is dying, maybe it’s because it’s not fun any more. You should quit. You don’t owe anyone anything. Homebrew maintainers are encouraged to leave without guilt or explanation.

sentences.en: If your project is dying, maybe it’s because it’s not fun any more.
sentences.zh: 如果你的项目正在消亡，也许是因为它不再有趣了。

sentences.en: You should quit.
sentences.zh: 你应该退出。

sentences.en: You don’t owe anyone anything.
sentences.zh: 你不欠任何人任何东西。

sentences.en: Homebrew maintainers are encouraged to leave without guilt or explanation.
sentences.zh: 鼓励自制软件维护者在没有任何负罪感或解释的情况下离开。

blocks.html_en: If you don’t want to quit (or if you’re on a project where you don’t want others to quit) and things are going badly: change something. Don’t just ask for more money or sponsors or donations. That will not magically make things fun again. Getting more money is not in your locus of control.

sentences.en: If you don’t want to quit (or if you’re on a project where you don’t want others to quit) and things are going badly: change something.
sentences.zh: 如果你不想退出（或者如果你正在进行一个你不希望其他人退出的项目）并且事情进展得很糟糕：改变一些东西。

sentences.en: Don’t just ask for more money or sponsors or donations.
sentences.zh: 不要只是要求更多的钱、赞助商或捐款。

sentences.en: That will not magically make things fun again.
sentences.zh: 这不会神奇地让事情再次变得有趣。

sentences.en: Getting more money is not in your locus of control.
sentences.zh: 获得更多的钱不在你的控制范围之内。

blocks.html_en: Instead: stop doing the parts of your project that are not fun. Maybe that’s stable releases. Maybe that’s release notes. Maybe that’s backwards compatibility. Whatever it is: again, you don’t owe anyone anything. You can do OSS however the hell you want to do it.

sentences.en: Instead: stop doing the parts of your project that are not fun.
sentences.zh: 相反：停止做项目中不有趣的部分。

sentences.en: Maybe that’s stable releases.
sentences.zh: 也许那是稳定版本。

sentences.en: Maybe that’s release notes.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是发行说明。

sentences.en: Maybe that’s backwards compatibility.
sentences.zh: 也许这就是向后兼容性。

sentences.en: Whatever it is: again, you don’t owe anyone anything.
sentences.zh: 不管是什么：再说一次，你不欠任何人任何东西。

sentences.en: You can do OSS however the hell you want to do it.
sentences.zh: 不管你想做什么，你都可以做 OSS。

blocks.html_en: People running soup kitchens don’t get constant complaints that the soup tastes like shit. They aren’t critiqued for not providing the optimum macronutrient balance. They do what they can. How sad is it, then, that some very well-compensated open source users with tech jobs treat volunteers so poorly?

sentences.en: People running soup kitchens don’t get constant complaints that the soup tastes like shit.
sentences.zh: 经营流动厨房的人不会经常抱怨汤的味道很糟糕。

sentences.en: They aren’t critiqued for not providing the optimum macronutrient balance.
sentences.zh: 他们不会因为没有提供最佳的常量营养素平衡而受到批评。

sentences.en: They do what they can.
sentences.zh: 他们尽其所能。

sentences.en: How sad is it, then, that some very well-compensated open source users with tech jobs treat volunteers so poorly?
sentences.zh: 那么，一些报酬丰厚、从事技术工作的开源用户对待志愿者的态度如此恶劣，这是多么可悲的事情？

blocks.html_en: ⏭️ OK, What Now?

sentences.en: ⏭️ OK, What Now?
sentences.zh: ⏭️ 好的，现在怎么办？

blocks.html_en: Are you a maintainer? If so, consider what keeps maintaining your project fun or what would make it fun again. If it isn’t fun and you can’t make it fun again: quit.

sentences.en: Are you a maintainer?
sentences.zh: 你是维护者吗？

sentences.en: If so, consider what keeps maintaining your project fun or what would make it fun again.
sentences.zh: 如果是这样，请考虑一下是什么让你的项目保持乐趣或者什么会让它再次变得有趣。

sentences.en: If it isn’t fun and you can’t make it fun again: quit.
sentences.zh: 如果它不有趣并且你无法让它再次变得有趣：退出。

blocks.html_en: Are you a contributor? Ensure that you’re having fun contributing but not in a way that makes it less fun for the maintainers. If you’re submitting AI-generated content, carefully review and test it. Speak to the human maintainers instead of deferring to your LLM.

sentences.en: Are you a contributor?
sentences.zh: 您是贡献者吗？

sentences.en: Ensure that you’re having fun contributing but not in a way that makes it less fun for the maintainers.
sentences.zh: 确保你享受贡献的乐趣，但不会让维护者失去乐趣。

sentences.en: If you’re submitting AI-generated content, carefully review and test it.
sentences.zh: 如果您要提交人工智能生成的内容，请仔细检查和测试。

sentences.en: Speak to the human maintainers instead of deferring to your LLM.
sentences.zh: 与人类维护人员交谈，而不是听从你的法学硕士。

blocks.html_en: Are you a user? If you’re filing a bug report, take your time and provide all the requested information. Most importantly: be grateful for the gift of open source you’re getting for free. Keep your rants for the pub or coffee shop and off the internet. Drive-by negativity kills open source.

sentences.en: Are you a user?
sentences.zh: 您是用户吗？

sentences.en: If you’re filing a bug report, take your time and provide all the requested information.
sentences.zh: 如果您要提交错误报告，请花点时间提供所有要求的信息。

sentences.en: Most importantly: be grateful for the gift of open source you’re getting for free.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是：感谢您免费获得的开源礼物。

sentences.en: Keep your rants for the pub or coffee shop and off the internet.
sentences.zh: 不要在互联网上发表对酒吧或咖啡店的咆哮。

sentences.en: Drive-by negativity kills open source.
sentences.zh: 盲目的消极情绪扼杀了开源。

blocks.html_en: Are you a company consuming open source? Allow your employees to participate in Open Source Friday. Alternatively, look the other way when they participate in the Open Source Resistance. Sponsor some projects you rely on.

sentences.en: Are you a company consuming open source?
sentences.zh: 您是一家使用开源的公司吗？

sentences.en: Allow your employees to participate in Open Source Friday.
sentences.zh: 允许您的员工参加开源星期五活动。

sentences.en: Alternatively, look the other way when they participate in the Open Source Resistance.
sentences.zh: 或者，当他们参与开源抵抗运动时，以另一种方式看待。

sentences.en: Sponsor some projects you rely on.
sentences.zh: 赞助一些您依赖的项目。

blocks.html_en: Keep having fun and the open source community will outlive us all.

sentences.en: Keep having fun and the open source community will outlive us all.
sentences.zh: 继续享受乐趣，开源社区将比我们所有人更长久。

sentences.en: Thanks to John Peebles, Graeme Arthur, Patrick Linnane, Andrew Nesbitt and Lindsay McQuaid for reviewing this post and providing helpful feedback.
sentences.zh: 感谢 John Peebles、Graeme Arthur、Patrick Linnane、Andrew Nesbitt 和 Lindsay McQuaid 审阅本文并提供有用的反馈。

sentences.en: Written by me, not an AI.
sentences.zh: 是我写的，不是AI。

sentences.zh: 我会征求人工智能的建议，并仅在我同意的情况下才提出申请（通常我不同意）。

content_html_zh:
26 July 2026

几周前，我与一群参与其他著名开源项目的人进行了一次电话会议。 组织者开玩笑地要求我们举手，如果前六个月比以前更好。 我举起了手。 没有其他人这样做。 为什么？ 我维护 Homebrew（适用于所有地方的包管理器）已经近 17 年了。 在那段时间里，我花了绝大多数时间都在做这件事，而且我从未精疲力尽。 我比以往任何时候都更有趣。

当前围绕开源的叙述令人沮丧。 显然是“死”了。

AI 路过问题、拉取请求和安全报告让维护人员难以承受。 不断提高的安全期望（感谢 Mythos）要求维护人员做更多的工作。 开源资金难以获得且不足。

其中一些正在发生，但我确信在 Homebrew 中看不到它。 另一位 Homebrew 维护者告诉我：

我比以前更开心了。

💎 最稀缺的资源

正如我之前所写，开源中最稀缺的资源不是金钱，而是维护者的动力。 今天向 Homebrew 发送 1000 美元并不会神奇地创造更多维护者时间（但如果您能负担得起，请捐赠以资助 Homebrew 的基础设施、津贴、赠款和聚会）。 我们都有不维护 Homebrew 的工作。 如果我们积极维护 Homebrew，我们会收到少量资金（300 美元/月）。 这不是“市场小时费率”。 许多送报纸的孩子的小时费率更高。

存在阈值效应：如果资金让维护人员减少带薪工作时间或辞职，资金只会创造更多时间。 维护者不想做的工作是付费合同的良好候选者。 如果你无法资助它：不要这样做。

那么为什么要这样做呢？ 乐趣。

并非所有事情都一直很有趣，但它需要是“功利的净乐趣”：总体而言，比不有趣更有趣。 这主要是关于志愿者运行的开源，但仅此而已。 如果你有一份带薪开源工作并且讨厌它：你也应该辞职。

这是一个周日的下午。 昨天大部分时间我都带着孩子们，所以今天我有一点“自己”的时间。 我花了很多时间在 Homebrew 上。 不是因为我“必须”这样做；而是因为我“不得不”这样做。没有什么紧急的事情进来。 不是因为“供应链”。 不是因为钱。 因为我想这么做。 因为这很有趣。

我第一次真正体验 OSS 是在一个成功的、成熟的项目中，我可以观察到它的文化。 这就是 KDE，Linux 桌面环境背后的社区。 2009 年，我参加了 Akademy（KDE 贡献者会议）和 GUADEC（GNOME 贡献者会议），这两个会议均在加那利群岛举行。

首先，这很奇怪，因为如果你在网上阅读这些讨论，你通常会站在“KDE SUCKS，GNOME ROCKS”或“GNOME SUCKS，KDE ROCKS”阵营。 然而：两个团队一起工作。 不仅仅是一起工作，还有吃、喝、社交和建立新的友谊。

其次，我可以看出，对于 KDE 阵营中的许多人来说，这些都是他们的人，这是他们这一年的亮点。 他们回来后精神焕发，并积极致力于 KDE 工作。 大多数人并没有得到报酬来修复、维护或编写 KDE 代码。 他们似乎也没有为用户做这件事。 他们这样做是因为他们很开心，既可以单独编写代码，也可以帮助他们的朋友构建他们关心的东西。

在过去的几年里，Homebrew 维护者每年都会在布鲁塞尔与 FOSDEM 共同举办的“Homebrew AGM”上举行会议。 我们见面、吃饭、喝酒、社交并为 Homebrew 制定计划。 之后，我们又充满活力地回来了。 自从我们开始这样做以来，我还看到人们为其他维护者做的事情比直接为用户做的更多。 开源超越国界：我们大多数人并不关心另一个维护者来自哪个国家或他们是什么国籍，只关心我们是朋友，一起构建我们觉得有趣的东西。 这些关系很重要，因为没有维护者，项目就死了。

🍺 保持自制的乐趣

这就是为什么我一直热衷于 Homebrew 成为一个有趣的项目。 处理正当行为并不有趣。 设置 SLA 并不有趣。 保持无限期的向后兼容性并不有趣。

Homebrew 之所以成功，是因为有趣、自动化、社区和将维护人员放在第一位，从一开始就是优先考虑的事情。 具体来说，我们自动评论评论，这样机器人就可以成为学究，而人类可以专注于同理心。 我们的护栏包括 CI、linting、打字和测试，以便在维护人员指出之前发现常规错误。 功能标志和分阶段推出让我们能够在不破坏每个人的情况下进行实验。 这意味着维护人员可以花更少的时间进行重复性修正，而将更多的时间花在他们感兴趣的工作上。

AI 擅长枯燥的工作，例如编写 CI 工作流程、linter 和文档。 这些实践对人工智能和人类贡献者都有帮助。 维护者可以使用或避免人工智能，以更好地保持他们的动力为准。

如果您在阅读毫不费力的人工智能生成的内容时目光呆滞：请在没有评论或理由的情况下关闭它，并阻止那些不学习或改进的惯犯。 在 Homebrew，我们的拉取请求模板要求贡献者披露 AI 使用情况，CI 作业会自动关闭模板不完整的拉取请求。 在没有我们的模板的情况下通过 API 提出的问题或 PR 通常表明人工智能的使用缺乏人工参与。

🛑 停止、付款或退出

自制啤酒正在蓬勃发展，而不是消亡。 它有 28 名活跃维护者。 一年前有 29 名维护者，现在只剩下 26 名。 根据我们的治理规则，我们会在维护者连续两个季度未达到活动阈值后将其删除。

如果你的项目正在消亡，也许是因为它不再有趣了。 你应该退出。 你不欠任何人任何东西。 鼓励自制软件维护者在没有任何负罪感或解释的情况下离开。

如果你不想退出（或者如果你正在进行一个你不希望其他人退出的项目）并且事情进展得很糟糕：改变一些东西。 不要只是要求更多的钱、赞助商或捐款。 这不会神奇地让事情再次变得有趣。 获得更多的钱不在你的控制范围之内。

相反：停止做项目中不有趣的部分。 也许那是稳定版本。 也许这就是发行说明。 也许这就是向后兼容性。 不管是什么：再说一次，你不欠任何人任何东西。 不管你想做什么，你都可以做 OSS。

经营流动厨房的人不会经常抱怨汤的味道很糟糕。 他们不会因为没有提供最佳的常量营养素平衡而受到批评。 他们尽其所能。 那么，一些报酬丰厚、从事技术工作的开源用户对待志愿者的态度如此恶劣，这是多么可悲的事情？

⏭️ 好的，现在怎么办？

你是维护者吗？ 如果是这样，请考虑一下是什么让你的项目保持乐趣或者什么会让它再次变得有趣。 如果它不有趣并且你无法让它再次变得有趣：退出。

您是贡献者吗？ 确保你享受贡献的乐趣，但不会让维护者失去乐趣。 如果您要提交人工智能生成的内容，请仔细检查和测试。 与人类维护人员交谈，而不是听从你的法学硕士。

您是用户吗？ 如果您要提交错误报告，请花点时间提供所有要求的信息。 最重要的是：感谢您免费获得的开源礼物。 不要在互联网上发表对酒吧或咖啡店的咆哮。 盲目的消极情绪扼杀了开源。

您是一家使用开源的公司吗？ 允许您的员工参加开源星期五活动。 或者，当他们参与开源抵抗运动时，以另一种方式看待。 赞助一些您依赖的项目。
